Variance-covariance matrix of a LaMaModel object

vcov.LaMaModel.Rd

Computes the approximate covariance matrix of the estimated parameters coef(object), either as the inverse Hessian of the negative log-likelihood at the estimate (type = "hessian"), or as a heteroskedasticity and autocorrelation consistent (HAC) sandwich (type = "HAC"), which remains valid if the model is misspecified.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'LaMaModel'
vcov(object, type = c("hessian", "HAC"), lag = NULL, ...)

Arguments

object

model object of class "LaMaModel"

type

"hessian" (default) for the inverse Hessian, or "HAC" for the HAC sandwich

lag

bandwidth \(L\) of the HAC sandwich, i.e. the maximum lag of the autocovariances included. Defaults to the rule of thumb above. lag = 0 gives the ordinary (heteroskedasticity robust) sandwich.

...

additional arguments (not used)

Value

covariance matrix with rows and columns named like coef(object)

Details

Hessian. The Hessian \(H\) is

  • the exact Hessian obj$he() for models without random effects,

  • for models with random effects, the Hessian of the Laplace-approximated marginal likelihood w.r.t. the fixed parameters, by finite differences of obj$gr() (as in sdreport),

  • for models from qreml, the Hessian of the penalised negative log-likelihood, including the penalised coefficients. The covariance is then conditional on the estimated smoothing parameters.

If the Hessian is not positive definite, which indicates that the model has not converged, a warning is issued.

HAC sandwich. With the per-observation score contributions \(u_t\) from scores, the covariance is \(H^{-1} M H^{-1}\), with the Newey-West (Bartlett kernel) estimate $$M = \Gamma_0 + \sum_{l=1}^{L} \Bigl(1 - \frac{l}{L+1}\Bigr) (\Gamma_l + \Gamma_l^\top), \qquad \Gamma_l = \sum_t u_t u_{t-l}^\top,$$ where the sum in \(\Gamma_l\) only runs over pairs of observations from the same track (as reported by forward), as different tracks are independent. Missing observations contribute zero scores, so lags remain in units of time. The default bandwidth is \(L = \lfloor 4 (\bar T / 100)^{2/9} \rfloor\), with \(\bar T\) the mean track length.

If the model is correctly specified, the \(u_t\) are martingale differences, so \(\Gamma_l \approx 0\) for \(l \ge 1\) and \(M \approx H\): both types then agree approximately, and marked differences point to misspecification. The HAC sandwich requires the likelihood function to call forward once (with trackID for several tracks) and is not available for models with random effects or from qreml.

References

Newey, W. K. and West, K. D. (1987). A simple, positive semi-definite, heteroskedasticity and autocorrelation consistent covariance matrix. Econometrica, 55(3), 703–708.
